name: Rehoboam
charge: Forsaking the counsel of the old men; forsaking the law of the Lord
summary: Solomon's son rejected the elders' advice to serve the people and took his young companions' line: my little finger shall be thicker than my father's loins. Ten tribes left him that day. Later, when the kingdom was established, he forsook the law of the Lord and all Israel with him.
offense: The people came to Rehoboam at Shechem asking that he lighten the grievous service and heavy yoke laid upon them under Solomon. They offered to serve him if he would hear their burden (1 Kings 12:1-5). The new king asked for three days before answering. Taking time for counsel was sound; the failure came in choosing which counsel would govern him. The elders who had stood before Solomon told him to serve the people that day and answer with good words. His companions told him to announce a heavier yoke and scorpions in place of whips (1 Kings 12:6-11). One answer sought an enduring bond through service. The other treated the people's distress as an opportunity to display superiority. Proverbs 15:1 sets a soft answer against grievous words that stir up anger. Rehoboam chose the rough answer. Possession of the throne had not given him the understanding by which it could be held. Later, after he established and strengthened the kingdom, he forsook the law, and the people followed him (2 Chronicles 12:1). The repeated failure was a heart that had not prepared itself to seek the Lord (2 Chronicles 12:14). Neither inherited position nor strengthened cities supplied that preparation.
judgment: The northern tribes rejected the house of David, stoned Adoram, and made Jeroboam king. Rehoboam fled to Jerusalem (1 Kings 12:16-20). His answer fulfilled the division already declared through Ahijah, yet the prophecy did not make his pride wise. The Lord accomplished his word through a king responsible for the answer he chose. When Rehoboam assembled Judah and Benjamin to recover the kingdom, Shemaiah forbade them to fight their brethren because the division was from the Lord. They obeyed and returned (1 Kings 12:21-24). He could still hearken to correction after refusing sound counsel at Shechem. Shishak afterward took Judah's fortified cities and threatened Jerusalem. Shemaiah named the cause: because they had forsaken the Lord, he had left them in Shishak's hand. The king and princes humbled themselves and confessed that the Lord was righteous (2 Chronicles 12:2-6). The Lord granted some deliverance, but they would serve Shishak and learn the difference between his service and the service of earthly kingdoms (2 Chronicles 12:7-8). Egypt carried away the treasures and Solomon's golden shields; Rehoboam replaced the gold with brass. Humbling preserved him from utter destruction without restoring everything his departure had cost.

verses.text: And king Rehoboam consulted with the old men, that stood before Solomon his father while he yet lived, and said, How do ye advise that I may answer this people?
And they spake unto him, saying, If thou wilt be a servant unto this people this day, and wilt serve them, and answer them, and speak good words to them, then they will be thy servants for ever.
But he forsook the counsel of the old men, which they had given him, and consulted with the young men that were grown up with him, and which stood before him:
And he said unto them, What counsel give ye that we may answer this people, who have spoken to me, saying, Make the yoke which thy father did put upon us lighter?

And the young men that were grown up with him spake unto him, saying, Thus shalt thou speak unto this people that spake unto thee, saying, Thy father made our yoke heavy, but make thou it lighter unto us; thus shalt thou say unto them, My little finger shall be thicker than my father’s loins.
And now whereas my father did lade you with a heavy yoke, I will add to your yoke: my father hath chastised you with whips, but I will chastise you with scorpions.
So Jeroboam and all the people came to Rehoboam the third day, as the king had appointed, saying, Come to me again the third day.
And the king answered the people roughly, and forsook the old men’s counsel that they gave him;

And spake to them after the counsel of the young men, saying, My father made your yoke heavy, and I will add to your yoke: my father also chastised you with whips, but I will chastise you with scorpions.
Wherefore the king hearkened not unto the people; for the cause was from the Lord, that he might perform his saying, which the Lord spake by Ahijah the Shilonite unto Jeroboam the son of Nebat.

So when all Israel saw that the king hearkened not unto them, the people answered the king, saying, What portion have we in David? neither have we inheritance in the son of Jesse: to your tents, O Israel: now see to thine own house, David. So Israel departed unto their tents.
And it came to pass, when Rehoboam had established the kingdom, and had strengthened himself, he forsook the law of the Lord, and all Israel with him.
And it came to pass, that in the fifth year of king Rehoboam Shishak king of Egypt came up against Jerusalem, because they had transgressed against the Lord,

Then came Shemaiah the prophet to Rehoboam, and to the princes of Judah, that were gathered together to Jerusalem because of Shishak, and said unto them, Thus saith the Lord, Ye have forsaken me, and therefore have I also left you in the hand of Shishak.
Whereupon the princes of Israel and the king humbled themselves; and they said, The Lord is righteous.

And when the Lord saw that they humbled themselves, the word of the Lord came to Shemaiah, saying, They have humbled themselves; therefore I will not destroy them, but I will grant them some deliverance; and my wrath shall not be poured out upon Jerusalem by the hand of Shishak.
Nevertheless they shall be his servants; that they may know my service, and the service of the kingdoms of the countries.

So Shishak king of Egypt came up against Jerusalem, and took away the treasures of the house of the Lord, and the treasures of the king’s house; he took all: he carried away also the shields of gold which Solomon had made.
And he did evil, because he prepared not his heart to seek the Lord.

And Rehoboam the son of Solomon reigned in Judah. Rehoboam was forty and one years old when he began to reign, and he reigned seventeen years in Jerusalem, the city which the Lord did choose out of all the tribes of Israel, to put his name there. And his mother’s name was Naamah an Ammonitess.
And Judah did evil in the sight of the Lord, and they provoked him to jealousy with their sins which they had committed, above all that their fathers had done.
For they also built them high places, and images, and groves, on every high hill, and under every green tree.
And there were also sodomites in the land: and they did according to all the abominations of the nations which the Lord cast out before the children of Israel.
And it came to pass in the fifth year of king Rehoboam, that Shishak king of Egypt came up against Jerusalem:
And he took away the treasures of the house of the Lord, and the treasures of the king’s house; he even took away all: and he took away all the shields of gold which Solomon had made.

Thus rested Solomon with his fathers, and of his seed he left behind him Roboam, even the foolishness of the people, and one that had no understanding, who turned away the people through his counsel. There was also Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who caused Israel to sin, and shewed Ephraim the way of sin:

entries.commentary: Rehoboam went to Shechem, where all Israel came to make him king. Jeroboam, still in Egypt, heard of it and returned, and the congregation of Israel came to Rehoboam asking him to lighten the grievous yoke and heavy service his father had put on them. The heavy yoke was the labor of the building; Solomon did not enslave his own people as he did the other nations, but they did have to put in that work. Rehoboam told them to depart three days and return, which was wisdom, for it is right to take time and get counsel before giving an answer.

Rehoboam consulted the old men that stood before Solomon his father, who advised that if he would be a servant to the people and speak good words, they would be his servants forever, but he forsook their counsel and consulted the young men he grew up with. Solomon was the wisest man on earth and still had counselors, yet Rehoboam forsook the counselors of the wisest man for his peers. The problem is getting counsel from those on your own level rather than from elders. The young men told him to say his little finger would be thicker than his father's loins, and that where his father chastised them with whips he would chastise them with scorpions, which was disrespectful.

When Jeroboam and the people came the third day, Rehoboam answered roughly, forsaking the old men's counsel, and told them he would add to their yoke and chastise them with scorpions. The king hearkened not to the people, for the cause was from the Most High, that he might perform the saying he spoke by Ahijah the Shilonite to Jeroboam; the prophecy had to come to pass.

When all Israel saw the king would not hearken, they said, What portion have we in David? To your tents, O Israel. So Israel departed and rebelled against the house of David to this day, and only over those in the cities of Judah did Rehoboam reign. Rehoboam sent Adoram who was over the tribute, and all Israel stoned him with stones, so the king fled in his chariot to Jerusalem. This is the split, the northern tribes rebelling against the house of David until this day. When Israel heard Jeroboam had returned, they called him to the congregation and made him king over Israel; none followed the house of David but the tribe of Judah only. That is how Jeroboam got the ten tribes.

Rehoboam assembled the house of Judah with Benjamin, a hundred and eighty thousand chosen warriors, to fight against the house of Israel and bring the kingdom back to himself. But the word of the Most High came to Shemaiah the man of God, telling Rehoboam and the house of Judah and Benjamin not to fight against their brethren the children of Israel, for this thing was from the Most High; and they hearkened and returned home.

Jeroboam built Shechem in mount Ephraim and Penuel, and feared in his heart that if the people went up to sacrifice at Jerusalem their hearts would turn again to Rehoboam king of Judah and they would kill him. Jeroboam took counsel and made two calves of gold, telling Israel it was too much to go up to Jerusalem, and setting one calf in Bethel and the other in Dan, and this thing became a sin. He made a house of high places and priests of the lowest of the people, not of the sons of Levi. Jeroboam ordained a feast in the eighth month on the fifteenth day, a feast he devised of his own heart, and offered on the altar at Bethel sacrificing to the calves he made. Devising your own holy days and throwing off the days of the Most High is the same error men make today, and after forty years of peace under Solomon the nation of Israel began to decline even more.

When Rehoboam establishes the kingdom and strengthens himself, he forsakes the law of the Lord, and all Israel with him. One who leads goes astray and carries many others with him; this is why the people must be examples to one another in righteousness, of one mind and one spirit in the rebuilding of the kingdom.

In the fifth year of Rehoboam, Shishak king of Egypt comes up against Jerusalem because Rehoboam transgressed against the Lord. Shishak comes with twelve hundred chariots, threescore thousand horsemen, and people without number out of Egypt, the Lubims, the Sukkiims, and the Ethiopians. He takes the fenced cities of Judah and comes to Jerusalem; the invasion is the direct result of forsaking the law.

Shemaiah the prophet comes to Rehoboam and the princes of Judah gathered at Jerusalem and declares the word of the Lord: because they have forsaken him, he has left them in the hand of Shishak. The princes and the king humble themselves and say the Lord is righteous. When correction comes, the right response is to confess that the Most High is righteous in what he does, acknowledging the punishment as just.

When the Lord sees that they humble themselves, his word comes to Shemaiah saying he will not destroy them but grant them some deliverance, and his wrath will not be poured on Jerusalem by the hand of Shishak. Nevertheless they will be Shishak's servants, that they may know the difference between serving the Most High and serving the kingdoms of the countries. The people today must likewise humble themselves, relearn to obey the commandments, and accept their condition as righteous judgment from the hand of the Most High. -

Shishak takes away the treasures of the house of the Lord and of the king's house, carrying off all the shields of gold Solomon had made. Rehoboam makes shields of brass in their place and commits them to the guard that keeps the entrance of the king's house. Whenever the king enters the house of the Lord the guard fetches the shields and returns them to the guard chamber.

Because Rehoboam humbles himself, the wrath of the Lord turns from him so that he is not utterly destroyed, and in Judah things go well. Deliverance and the destruction of enemies come to the people when they humble themselves before the Most High.

Rehoboam strengthens himself in Jerusalem and reigns; he is forty and one years old when he begins to reign and reigns seventeen years in Jerusalem, the city the Lord chose to put his name there. His mother's name is Naamah an Ammonitess. He does evil because he prepares not his heart to seek the Lord; the failure is a heart never set on the Most High.

The acts of Rehoboam are written in the book of Shemaiah the prophet and of Iddo the seer concerning genealogies, and there were wars between Rehoboam and Jeroboam continually. Rehoboam sleeps with his fathers, is buried in the city of David, and his son Abijah reigns in his place. The account then turns to Abijah's rule over Judah in the next chapter, continuing this compressed history that is told more fully in 1 and 2 Kings. --- Topics: [Idolatry](/encyclopedia/idolatry) · [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement) · [The Covenant](/encyclopedia/the-covenant) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood)

When Jeroboam's son Abijah falls sick, the king tells his wife to disguise herself and go to Ahijah the prophet in Shiloh, carrying loaves, cakes, and honey to inquire about the child. Ahijah is old and blind, but the Most High tells him beforehand that Jeroboam's wife is coming feigning to be another woman. The moment he hears her feet at the door, Ahijah calls her by name and says he is sent to her with heavy tidings.

The message declares that though the Most High exalted Jeroboam from among the people and rent the kingdom from the house of David to give it to him, he did not walk as David who kept the commandments. Instead he made other gods and molten images and cast the Most High behind his back, doing evil above all before him. Therefore the Most High will bring evil on his house, cut off every male, and sweep away the remnant as a man sweeps away dung until it is gone. -
Jeroboam made other gods and molten images and cast the Most High behind his back.

Ahijah tells the wife that when her feet enter the city, the child will die, and all Israel will mourn and bury him, for in him alone of Jeroboam's house is found some good thing toward the Most High. The Most High will raise up a king to cut off the house of Jeroboam and will scatter Israel beyond the river because they made their groves and provoked Him to anger. As soon as she reaches the threshold of her house, the child dies, exactly as spoken by the hand of Ahijah, and all Israel mourns.

Jeroboam reigned twenty-two years, then slept with his fathers, and Nadab his son reigned in his place. In Judah, Rehoboam, forty-one at his accession, reigned seventeen years in Jerusalem, and Judah did evil and provoked the Most High to jealousy above all their fathers. They built high places, images, and groves on every hill, and there were also sodomites in the land, doing according to the abominations of the nations cast out before them. -

In Rehoboam's fifth year, Shishak king of Egypt comes against Jerusalem and takes the treasures of the house of the Most High and the king's house, including the gold shields Solomon made. Rehoboam replaces the gold shields with brass, marking Israel's fall from gold to brass, from the riches of Solomon's day to loss. There is continual war between Rehoboam and Jeroboam, and when Rehoboam dies, Abijam his son reigns in his place.

lawsResolved.text: Leaders chosen must be wise and just.
Civil authorities who are oppressive do not understand justice.
Pride and arrogance brings decline, punishment and destruction.
Warnings of the iniquity of turning from God.
The way of a fool is right in his own eyes, but he who heeds counsel is wise.
